From Bill Demchak, PNC Chairman and Chief Executive Officer: “Our strategy continues to drive growth across our businesses, as we deepen our presence in key markets and expand our reach nationally. During the third quarter, we continued to build on the strong momentum we delivered in the first half of the year, and we generated an 18.3% return on average tangible common equity. We are well positioned, and remain confident in our long-term outlook.” - more - PNC Reports Third Quarter 2026 Net Income of $2.1 Billion, $4.97 Diluted EPS or $5.09 As Adjusted – Page 2 Integration Costs and Significant Items In the third quarter of 2026, PNC incurred integration costs related to the FirstBank acquisition of $36 million. Results also included significant items of negative $25 million related to net Visa activity, including an $11 million valuation gain on remaining Visa shares received in the second quarter exchange and negative $36 million of Visa Class B-3 derivative fair value adjustments, primarily related to litigation escrow funding. The combined after-tax impact of both integration costs and 3Q26 significant items resulted in a $48 million decline in net income, or a 12 cent reduction to EPS. During the second quarter of 2026, PNC incurred integration costs of $127 million and significant items with a net benefit of $84 million, as outlined in the table below. The combined after-tax impact of both integration costs and 2Q26 significant items resulted in a $15 million decline in net income, or a 4 cent reduction to EPS. Income Statement Highlights Third quarter 2026 compared with second quarter 2026 ▪ Total revenue of $6.6 billion decreased $313 million, or 5%, as growth in net interest income was more than offset by lower noninterest income. – Net interest income of $4.2 billion increased $99 million, or 2%, driven by commercial loan growth and higher yields on interest-earning assets, partially offset by increased funding costs. • Net interest margin of 2.94% decreased 2 basis points. – Fee income of $2.1 billion decreased $137 million, or 6%, primarily due to elevated second quarter capital markets and advisory revenue. – Other noninterest income of $214 million included higher private equity revenue and significant items of negative $25 million related to net Visa activity. - more - PNC Reports Third Quarter 2026 Net Income of $2.1 Billion, $4.97 Diluted EPS or $5.09 As Adjusted – Page 3 ▪ Noninterest expense of $3.8 billion decreased $347 million, or 8%, and included $27 million of integration costs in the third quarter, compared to $261 million of both integration costs and significant items in the second quarter. Excluding these items from both quarters, noninterest expense, as adjusted, decreased 3%. ▪ Provision for credit losses was $189 million in the third quarter, stable from the second quarter. ▪ The effective tax rate was 20.0% for the third quarter and 20.5% for the second quarter. Balance Sheet Highlights Third quarter 2026 compared with second quarter 2026 or September 30, 2026 compared with June 30, 2026 ▪ Average loans of $372.2 billion increased $9.0 billion, or 2%. Average commercial loans increased $10.4 billion, or 4%, driven by strong new production and increased utilization. Average consumer loans decreased $1.4 billion, or 1%, primarily due to lower residential mortgage loans and the student loan portfolio transfer. – Loans at September 30, 2026 of $378.8 billion increased $10.8 billion, or 3%, from June 30, 2026, driven by commercial loan growth. This increase was partially offset by a decline in consumer loans, including the transfer of the $1.4 billion student loan portfolio to held-for-sale. ▪ Credit quality performance: – Delinquencies of $1.3 billion decreased $135 million, or 9%, due to lower consumer loan delinquencies. – Total nonperforming loans of $2.2 billion increased $167 million, or 8%, driven by higher commercial nonperforming loans. – Net loan charge-offs were $257 million and included $35 million related to the transfer of student loans to held-for-sale. – The allowance for credit losses was $5.4 billion, or 1.42% of total loans, at September 30, 2026 and $5.5 billion, or 1.48% of total loans, at June 30, 2026. ▪ Average investment securities of $151.4 billion increased $4.3 billion, or 3%, reflecting higher residential mortgage-backed securities. ▪ Average deposits of $461.2 billion increased $4.2 billion, or 1% , primarily due to seasonally higher commercial interest-bearing deposits . – Deposits at September 30, 2026 of $466.4 billion increased $16.6 billion, or 4%, from June 30, 2026, driven by higher commercial interest-bearing deposits, reflecting seasonality as well as new and expanded client relationships. ▪ PNC maintained a strong capital and liquidity position: – On October 2, 2026, the PNC board of directors declared a quarterly cash dividend on common stock of $2.00 per share to be paid on November 5, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business October 14, 2026. – PNC returned $1.4 billion of capital to shareholders, reflecting $0.8 billion of dividends on common shares and $0.6 billion of common share repurchases. – Share repurchase activity in the fourth quarter of 2026 is expected to approximate third quarter 2026 share repurchase levels. – The Basel III common equity tier 1 capital ratio was an estimated 9.8% at September 30, 2026 and was 9.9% at June 30, 2026. – PNC’s average LCR for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was 106%, exceeding reference.summary: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc. operates as a diversified financial services company in the United States. It operates through three segments: Retail Banking, Corporate & Institutional Banking, and Asset Management Group segments. The Retail Banking segment offers checking, savings, and money market accounts, and time deposit; residential mortgages, home equity loans and lines of credit, auto loans, credit cards, education loans, and personal and small business loans and lines of credit; and brokerage, insurance, and investment and cash management services. This segment serves consumer and small business customers through a network of branches, digital channels, ATMs, and through phone-based customer contact centers.
